title: Does MYP Prepare You for DP Geography or Economics?
summary: Learn how MYP Individuals and Societies prepares you for DP Geography or Economics, what changes in the Diploma, and how to prepare effectively.
body_markdown:
MYP Individuals and Societies provides a strong foundation for DP Geography and DP Economics through research, source evaluation, data interpretation, communication, and critical thinking. However, DP introduces specialized content, formal examinations, subject-specific terminology, and an internal assessment.


Preparation varies because schools may teach MYP Individuals and Societies as discrete, modular, or integrated courses. This means one student may have studied substantial economics while another focused on history or geography. Understanding your own strengths and gaps is therefore more useful than assuming MYP provides identical preparation everywhere.


### What MYP Individuals and Societies teaches you


The IB describes[MYP Individuals and Societies](https://ibo.org/programmes/middle-years-programme/curriculum/individuals-and-societies/) as an exploration of historical, geographical, political, social, economic, religious, technological, and cultural factors affecting societies and environments. Its breadth helps students investigate issues from several perspectives before specializing.


Four assessment criteria develop skills that remain valuable in DP:


- **Criterion A: Knowing and understanding** develops accurate knowledge and terminology.
- **Criterion B: Investigating** develops research questions, planning, evidence collection, and reflection.
- **Criterion C: Communicating** develops structured writing, appropriate formats, and source documentation.
- **Criterion D: Thinking critically** develops interpretation, source evaluation, argument, and consideration of perspectives.


Each criterion uses an **eight-point scale** in MYP. DP subjects do not retain this assessment structure, but students who can investigate a question, analyze evidence, and justify conclusions already possess important Group 3 skills.


### The transition from MYP Individuals and Societies to DP


The main change is from **breadth to disciplinary precision** . An MYP unit might connect migration, inequality, environmental pressure, and government policy. DP Geography or Economics examines such issues using the concepts, methods, terminology, and assessment conventions of one discipline.


Area MYP Individuals and Societies DP Geography or Economics


Curriculum Broad, flexible, and school-dependent Defined subject syllabus at SL or HL


Knowledge Concepts from several social sciences Detailed disciplinary knowledge


Assessment School tasks using four MYP criteria Subject examinations and internal assessment


Evidence Varied sources and interdisciplinary examples Geographic or economic evidence selected for the question


Writing Several formats and inquiry tasks Responses shaped by command terms and mark allocations


DP also requires sustained recall. Students must apply knowledge under timed conditions and distinguish command terms such as **describe** , **explain** , **analyse** , **compare** , and **evaluate** . Writing everything remembered about a topic rarely earns as much credit as selecting material that directly answers the question.


### How MYP prepares you for DP Geography


[DP Geography](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/curriculum/individuals-and-societies/geography/) examines relationships among people, places, environments, physical processes, and global change. MYP topics such as population, migration, urbanization, development, hazards, resources, climate, and sustainability provide useful foundations.


Transferable skills include interpreting maps, graphs, photographs, and statistics; comparing processes at different scales; examining stakeholder perspectives; and planning investigations. The main adjustment is using **specific geographic evidence** . Instead of stating that climate change affects poorer countries severely, a developed response explains the process, identifies a relevant place, supports the claim with accurate evidence, and recognizes differences among locations or social groups.


Geography also includes internal assessment work involving geographic investigation and fieldwork under the applicable course guide. MYP inquiry experience helps, but DP requires more precise methodology, data presentation, analysis, and conclusions. Students should confirm requirements for their examination session with their school.


### How MYP prepares you for DP Economics


[DP Economics](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/curriculum/individuals-and-societies/economics/) studies choices made when resources are scarce. Its major areas include microeconomics, macroeconomics, and the global economy, with theory applied to real situations and policies.


MYP work on markets, trade, globalization, development, inequality, sustainability, or government decisions can provide helpful context. Critical thinking also transfers because economists examine assumptions, consequences, stakeholder effects, and policy trade-offs.


The larger adjustment is using **economic models and diagrams precisely** . For example, explaining a tax may require a correctly labelled diagram, a clear chain of reasoning, application to a real situation, and evaluation of effects on consumers, producers, government, and other groups.


Economics requires numerical confidence, although it is not primarily an advanced mathematics course. Students should be comfortable with percentages, ratios, data tables, and step-by-step calculations. The official IB overview states that the internal assessment consists of **three commentaries based on published news extracts** , with key concepts used as analytical lenses.


### Which subject is the better match?


Neither subject is automatically easier. The better choice depends on the questions and evidence you prefer.


DP Geography may suit you if you enjoy DP Economics may suit you if you enjoy


People, places, environments, and spatial patterns Choices made by consumers, firms, and governments


Maps, fieldwork, statistics, and place-based examples Models, diagrams, data, and policy arguments


Population, climate, hazards, resources, and cities Markets, inflation, unemployment, trade, and development


Comparing processes across locations and scales Explaining incentives, consequences, and trade-offs


Geography is not simply memorizing case studies, while Economics is not simply drawing diagrams. Both demand explanation, evidence, application, and evaluation. Review your school’s course outline because available options, teaching order, fieldwork arrangements, and SL or HL expectations can influence your experience.


### A practical preparation plan


### Audit your MYP background


List previous units as geographic, economic, historical, political, or interdisciplinary. Compare them with introductory material from your future teacher to identify genuine gaps.


### Strengthen analytical writing


Practise paragraphs containing a claim, specific evidence, explanation, qualification, and judgment. Follow the command term: an **explanation** develops how or why something occurs, while an **evaluation** weighs evidence and reaches a justified conclusion.


### Review essential foundations


For Geography, revise scale, spatial distribution, population measures, development indicators, maps, and graphs. For Economics, review scarcity, opportunity cost, demand and supply, percentages, data interpretation, and diagram conventions. Secure understanding matters more than learning the full syllabus early.


### Build and apply an evidence bank


Geography students can record places, processes, scales, affected groups, and management responses. Economics students can record news events, concepts, models, stakeholders, outcomes, and evaluation points. Test yourself without notes rather than repeatedly rereading.


The[MYP Individuals and Societies resource hub](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp/myp-individuals-and-societies) and[Individuals and Societies cheatsheets](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp/myp-individuals-and-societies/cheatsheets) can support review. Prospective Economics students can use the[IB Economics resources](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-economics) , while the[IB subject resource collection](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib) provides broader Diploma support.


### Common preparation mistakes


Avoid memorizing definitions without applying them to a new graph, source, place, policy, or scenario. Other common mistakes include:


- Assuming a strong MYP grade guarantees the same DP result
- Ignoring command terms and writing everything known about a topic
- Treating examples as decoration rather than evidence
- Neglecting diagrams and quantitative skills in Economics
- Memorizing Geography case studies without understanding the process
- Using AI-generated material without checking accuracy or preserving personal authorship


The comparison of[MYP Individuals and Societies with DP Geography and Economics](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/myp-individuals-societies-vs-dp-geography-economics) further explains the assessment transition. This[review of RevisionDojo’s MYP resources](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/revisiondojo-myp-individuals-and-societies-review) shows how notes, recall, questions, and feedback can work together.


### Conclusion


MYP Individuals and Societies prepares students well for DP Geography or Economics by developing inquiry, communication, evidence analysis, and critical thinking. DP then requires deeper disciplinary knowledge, precise terminology, sustained recall, and subject-specific assessment skills.


Prepare by identifying gaps, strengthening analytical writing, reviewing foundational concepts, and applying knowledge to unfamiliar evidence. RevisionDojo Study Notes, Flashcards, Questionbank practice, and Jojo AI can support this work when used alongside independent thinking and teacher feedback.
